Зворотний слеш діє не лише з лапками: ко: The backslash works not only with quotation marks: the combination \\n means "start a new line here", and \\t means a tab, a jump to the next column. In the code, these are two characters, and in the line - one character, so the line remains one, even if it breaks up into several on the screen. It will not really work to move the text with ordinary quotation marks: Python will break the line and issue a SyntaxError: unterminated string literal. For text where every line is important, there are triple quotes - you can move the text with the Enter key itself, but \\n and \\t are fine everywhere. Tabs move the columns apart, but alignment is not guaranteed: different consoles give it a different pitch. And also: an empty print() is the same new line, only without text.

Кожен print автоматично додає наприкінці: Each print automatically appends a \\n to the end — so the next call starts a new line. end= replaces this end: print("a", end="") doesn't add anything, so print("b") is printed right after — leaving ab on one line. end=" " leaves a space, end="!" puts an exclamation mark instead of a break. end= is appropriate when the signature and value should be on the same line: print("Date:", end=" ") and then print(5, 11, 2026, sep=".") give "Date: 11/5/2026". Pay attention: end does not touch what is inside the call — sep is responsible for the spaces between values ​​and beyond.

Лапка для Python — не звичайний символ,: A quotation mark for Python is not an ordinary character, but a line boundary: the first quotation mark opens the line, the same one closes it. Therefore, in print("He says: "Hello""), Python will close the line before the word Hello and stop the program with a SyntaxError. In order for the quotation mark to become part of the text, a backslash is placed in front of it: \" — this is called escaping. There is a trick without a slash: to take the text in quotation marks of a different type — double quotation marks inside single ones are not considered a boundary, as well as an apostrophe inside double ones. But when the text contains both quotation marks and apostrophes, one pair will have to be escaped anyway. Another trick is to break the text into pieces and glue them through +, but the line becomes long and it's easy to lose a quotation mark in. Escaping leaves the text as a whole, which is read exactly as it is written, so it is shorter and more reliable.
